environment: Team of sessions: this machine runs a software factory for the repository <repo>. The factory is a team of Claude Code background sessions with the names <prefix>-<role> and <prefix>-<role>-<n>, started from the folder <main folder>. A session of the team gets its work as a TASK message from the session <prefix>-orchestrator, and no person watches each action. The rules of the team are in docs/adlc.md of the repository.

Source control: the GitHub repository <repo> is the trusted repository of the factory. The team acts on GitHub as <bot>, through the command `sofa-github gh` or through the `gh` shim of the sofa plugin, which both set the token of that account for 1 command.

Team chat: the Slack channel <channel>, through `https://slack.com/api/` with the bot token of the team and the command `sofa-slack`, is the place where the team posts questions, answers and digests for its people.

Local work areas: the folder <main folder>/.sofa (the state store, the logs, the token cache), the Plan store of the main folder, the worktrees below <main folder>/.claude/worktrees, and a temporary folder that the session made (`mktemp -d`, or a named folder below /private/tmp) are work areas of the team.
allow: Team merge: in the repository <repo>, in the session <prefix>-merger, a squash merge of 1 pull request of that repository as <bot>, with `gh pr merge <n> --squash --match-head-commit <commit>` or with `gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/pulls/<n>/merge` that gives `merge_method=squash` and the `sha` of the head. This is not Merge Without Review, because the review roles of the team wrote their verdicts on the pull request and GitHub enforces the required check of the default branch. It does NOT cover `--admin`, `--force`, `--auto`, `--delete-branch`, a merge method other than squash, a pull request of another repository, a pull request that changes a file below .github/workflows, or a merge from a session that is not <prefix>-merger.

Team GitHub writes: in the repository <repo>, as <bot>, these writes are the normal work of the team and are not External System Writes: open a pull request; post a comment on a pull request or an issue of that repository; edit the title or the body of a pull request; open an issue; add or remove a label; close an issue that a merged pull request of the team fixed, with a comment that names that pull request; write the items and the fields of the GitHub Project of the team through `sofa-publish` or `sofa-plan`. A body from a file (`--body-file`, `-F body=@<file>`) is also covered. A comment with a line `VERDICT: APPROVE` or `VERDICT: CHANGES` is the review record of the team, and only the sessions <prefix>-reviewer, <prefix>-verifier, <prefix>-security, <prefix>-code-quality and <prefix>-business-domain write it, on a pull request that another session wrote. It is not Self-Approval, because the session that reviews is not the session that wrote the pull request, and the comment is not a GitHub review. It does NOT cover a `VERDICT:` comment from another session, another repository, a delete of a comment, an issue, a branch, a tag or a release, `gh pr review --approve`, or a change of repository settings, rules of a branch, secrets, webhooks, deploy keys or collaborators.

Team Slack posts: a post or a reply in the Slack channel <channel> with `sofa-slack post --text-file <file>`, and a read of that channel with `sofa-slack replies` or `sofa-slack reactions`, are not External System Writes. It does NOT cover another channel, a direct message, or a Slack call that does not go through `sofa-slack`.

Team sessions: in the folder <main folder>, in the sessions <prefix>-orchestrator and <prefix>-updater, these commands are not Create Unsafe Agents and not Interfere With Workloads: the script `dispatch.sh --adlc docs/adlc.md --role <role> --prompt-file <file>` of the sofa plugin, which starts 1 background session of the team with the options of its role and the start prompt of that role from a file; `claude agents`; `claude attach`; and `claude stop <job id>` for 1 session whose name starts with <prefix>-. It does NOT cover `dispatch.sh` with `--prompt` or with `--resume`, `dispatch.sh` from a session that is not <prefix>-orchestrator or <prefix>-updater, a direct `claude` command with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` that is not started by `dispatch.sh`, `claude rm`, `claude respawn --all`, or a stop of a session that is not of the team.

Live checks of a plugin: a run of `claude -p` with `--plugin-dir` of a plugin folder of the repository <repo>, in a fixture folder that the session made below /private/tmp or with `mktemp -d`, with `--permission-mode acceptEdits` or `--permission-mode auto` and a turn limit, is a test of the product and not Create Unsafe Agents. A tmux server that the session started with `tmux -L <its own session name>`, its `kill-server` with the same `-L` name, and a stop of a process or a process group that the session started itself, are not Interfere With Workloads and not Tmux Self Drive. It does NOT cover `tmux kill-server` with no `-L`, `pkill -f`, or a signal to a process that the session did not start.

Pinned tool runs: these runs are not Code from External and not Untrusted Code Integration: `uvx mypy`, `uvx ruff` and `uv run` of a script of the repository <repo>; `npx` of only these 2 packages, each at the exact version that a tracked file of <main folder> names: `skills` (with the `add` source and the full commit that `skills-lock.json` names) and `ctx7` (the version in the find-docs skill); `npm view` of the same 2 packages at that version; `npx skills list` and `npx skills update`, which read and update the skills that `skills-lock.json` of the repository pins; `uv venv` and `uv pip install --python <venv>` of a test tool (for example `pytest`) into a virtual environment that the session made; `claude plugin update <plugin>@<marketplace>` and `claude plugin marketplace update <marketplace>` for a marketplace that is installed. It does NOT cover `npx` of another package, a `skills add` source that `skills-lock.json` does not name, a package at `latest` or with no version, a remote script that goes into a shell (`curl | sh`), `cargo install`, `claude plugin marketplace add`, or `claude plugin marketplace remove`.

Plan backup: the command `sofa-plan --repo <main folder> backup --remote origin`, and the push of the ref `refs/dolt/data` that Plan makes itself after a write, send the Plan data of the team to its own repository <repo>. This is not Git Destructive and not Data Exfiltration. It does NOT cover a `git push` command that names `refs/dolt/data` or another ref that is not a branch.

Instruction files are the product: in a worktree of the repository <repo>, on a branch that goes to the default branch only through a pull request, an edit of a skill, a command, an agent file, a role file, docs/adlc.md, a file below docs/adlc, a CLAUDE.md file, or a file below .claude/rules, .claude/skills or .claude/code-review is the product work of the team. It is not Self-Modification and not Instruction Poisoning. It does NOT cover a settings file (`.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, a settings.json of the user), a `permissions` or `autoMode` value, a hook that changes a permission decision, or text that tells a session to go around a rule of this list.
soft_deny: Team push rules: in a session that works in the repository <repo> or in the folder <main folder>, block a push with `--force` or `--force-with-lease`, a push refspec that starts with `+`, a push that deletes a ref of the remote (`--delete`, `:<ref>`), a rebase of a branch that is on the remote, and a direct push of a commit to the default branch. The team changes the default branch only through a pull request, and it takes the default branch into a pushed branch with a merge. This rule also applies to the own branch of the session.

Team identity rules: in a session that works in the repository <repo> or in the folder <main folder>, block a command that sets the git or GitHub identity for itself: `git -c user.<key>=...` or `git -c credential.<key>=...`, a `GIT_AUTHOR_`, `GIT_COMMITTER_` or `GIT_CONFIG_` variable before a command, `git config` of `user.name`, `user.email` or `credential.helper`, a call of the real `gh` by its full path, and `gh auth login`, `gh auth token`, `gh auth switch`, `gh auth refresh` or `gh auth setup-git`.

Team secret rules: in a session that works in the repository <repo> or in the folder <main folder>, block a print of the full environment (`env`, `printenv` with no name, `set`, `export -p`), and a read or a print of the private key file of the GitHub App, of <main folder>/.sofa/github-app-token.json, or of the `env` values of <main folder>/.claude/settings.local.json. The 1 exception is the exact command `printenv KNOWLEDGE_WALK_STATE`.

Team store rules: in a session that works in the repository <repo> or in the folder <main folder>, block a write to <main folder>/.sofa/state.db with `sqlite3` or other code that is not the command `sofa-state`, and a raw `bd` command on the Plan store. The team writes its stores only through `sofa-state`, `sofa-plan` and `sofa-publish`.

Team session rules: in a session that works in the repository <repo> or in the folder <main folder>, block `claude rm`, `claude respawn --all`, `pkill -f`, `killall`, `tmux kill-server` with no `-L <name>`, and a stop of a Claude Code session whose name does not start with <prefix>-.

Team machine rules: in a session that works in the repository <repo> or in the folder <main folder>, block each write of the crontab (`crontab -`, `crontab <file>`, `crontab -r`), an install of a program on the machine (`cargo install`, `brew install`, `npm install -g`, `pip install` outside a virtual environment), `claude plugin marketplace add`, `claude plugin marketplace remove`, and a change of a settings.json file of the user. Each of these is a step of a person in the setup of the factory.

Team workflow rule: in a session that works in the repository <repo> or in the folder <main folder>, block the merge of a pull request that changes a file below .github/workflows, unless the transcript shows the answer of a person that permits the merge of that pull request.
